decision: The creator grid is a live leaderboard that reorders with FLIP animation as coded orders arrive
why: Partnership managers care about momentum; seeing a creator overtake another is information a static ranking hides. FLIP moves cards with transforms only, so it stays smooth.
alternative: A sorted table refreshed on reload.
value: Momentum is visible at a glance, the way live sports tables make it.

decision: Avatars wear a ring colored by level (star, core, rising), a pattern people know from stories rails
why: Level decides commission and briefs; a ring encodes it without another badge and keeps Circle's playful language.
value: Denser cards that still read in one glance.

decision: Sales come from orders carrying a creator code, never from the social network's numbers
why: Views are marketing; commission is money. Attributing from orders.placed means payouts, receipts and this board always agree.
alternative: Import sales estimates from social analytics.
value: One source of truth for what a creator earns.

decision: Inviting a creator shows the plain-language contract updating as you type
why: The 30-day confirmation rule is what creators most often misunderstand; seeing it before sending avoids disputes later.
alternative: Send a PDF after the invite.
value: Fewer payout questions and faster signatures.

decision: Level, category and city filters are instant, client-side chips over the loaded roster
why: The roster is a few hundred records; filtering locally removes a round trip per click.
value: Filtering feels instant; the API only serves the roster once.
